column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “you shall not do” with the deeds of Egypt and Canaan; BSB says “you must not follow the practices.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes a relative of one’s “flesh” and says “uncover nakedness”; BSB uses “close relative” and “have sexual relations.”

The Hebrew joins “the nakedness of your father” and “the nakedness of your mother” with “and,” then repeats the uncovering prohibition. BSB interprets the connection with “by having sexual relations with your mother.”
The Hebrew repeats “nakedness,” saying the wife’s nakedness is the father’s nakedness; BSB interprets the final clause as dishonoring the father.
The Hebrew says “uncover their nakedness,” with a plural possessive for the alternatives; BSB uses “have sexual relations with your sister.”
The Hebrew says the granddaughters are “your nakedness”; BSB interprets this as bringing shame on “your family.”
The Hebrew repeats the nakedness expression at the beginning and end; BSB states the sexual-relations prohibition once.
The Hebrew says “uncover the nakedness” of the father’s sister; BSB says “have sexual relations with” her.
The Hebrew says “uncover the nakedness” of the mother’s sister; BSB says “have sexual relations with” her.
The Hebrew prohibits uncovering the uncle’s nakedness and approaching his wife; BSB interprets the first as dishonoring the uncle and adds “to have sexual relations with her” to the approach clause.
The Hebrew repeats “uncover nakedness” for the daughter-in-law; BSB uses “have sexual relations.”
The Hebrew identifies the wife’s nakedness as the brother’s nakedness; BSB interprets the final clause as shaming the brother.
The Hebrew uses “take” for the granddaughters and repeats the uncovering of nakedness; BSB specifies “marry” and “have sexual relations.”
The Hebrew says “uncover her nakedness”; BSB says “have sexual relations with her.”
The Hebrew says “uncover her nakedness”; BSB says “have sexual relations with her.”
The Hebrew includes the seed image in “give your lying for seed”; BSB says “lie carnally.”
The Hebrew says not to give one’s “seed” to be made to pass to Molech; BSB says not to give one’s “children” to be sacrificed.
The Hebrew uses plural “lyings of a woman”; BSB gives the comparison simply as “as with a woman.”
The Hebrew uses “give your lying” in the first prohibition; BSB says “lie carnally.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew narrates defilement, visitation of iniquity, and vomiting with past narrative forms; BSB shifts the punishment to “I am punishing” and the vomiting to “will vomit.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew says the land is not to vomit the people out when they defile it and names singular “the nation” previously expelled. BSB recasts this as an if-clause followed by a warning and uses plural “the nations.”
The Hebrew resumes plural “the persons who do them” after the opening “everyone who”; BSB keeps the offender singular throughout.
Close to the Hebrew.
